fixes.explanation: Good guess, baker, because the altar does come up earlier, back in verses 5 to 7. But when Moses and the Levitical priests speak to all Israel, they say, “Be silent, O Israel, and listen!” (Deuteronomy 27:9). Nobody is told to take a single step yet. First the crowd gets quiet, and then the hearing starts.

Yes, baker! Notice what's missing from that verse: no shoving, no tripping, nobody doing anything at all. The curse lands on the man who “lets a blind man wander in the road.” (Deuteronomy 27:18). So standing there and doing nothing counts. It's like watching a friend about to send a message to the wrong group chat and just letting it happen.

Yes, baker. Justice is the word, and the verb matters just as much: “withholds.” The curse is on the one who holds justice back from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow (Deuteronomy 27:19). Nothing here says he took anything. He kept it from them. And then, like every curse in this list, all the people answer, “Amen!”
